subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: Should externally or plugin-registered recurring agentTurn cron jobs require explicit operator activation and model/cost guardrails before they can run?
rationale: The source path is clear, but fixing it changes scheduler security boundaries, plugin scheduling API expectations, upgrade behavior, and provider quota policy.

options.title: Require explicit activation for external recurring agentTurn jobs
options.body: Preserve operator-created cron behavior where appropriate, but make externally/plugin-created recurring model-backed jobs carry trusted provenance, default disabled or pending, and require an explicit model or cost acknowledgment before running.

options.title: Keep enabled-by-default and document operator responsibility
options.body: Treat existing cron.add semantics as the compatibility contract and improve docs/doctor warnings without changing runtime activation behavior.

options.title: Defer to broader budget and provenance RFCs
options.body: Leave this issue open as dependent on #14376, #42475, and #71712 instead of shipping a targeted cron activation policy now.

recommendation.title: Require explicit activation for external recurring agentTurn jobs
recommendation.body: Preserve operator-created cron behavior where appropriate, but make externally/plugin-created recurring model-backed jobs carry trusted provenance, default disabled or pending, and require an explicit model or cost acknowledgment before running.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the most recent history across the current cron creation, plugin scheduling, and model-selection paths inspected for this issue.
